_help.auto_route: false = never switch brains; everything stays on the everyday model (settings.json 'model').
_help.coder_model: Takes over a coding task. Must be installed and able to call tools.
_help.deep_model: Writes a full plan (no tools) for a complex task.
_help.deep_runs: true = the deep model also carries out its own plan, but only if a test shows it really calls tools.
_help.heavy_model: Carries out a LONG plan with the tools instead of the everyday model (stronger with tools, slower).
_help.heavy_steps: A plan with MORE numbered steps than this goes to heavy_model. Higher = the everyday model does more.
_help.long_request_chars: A request longer than this many characters is treated as complex and gets a plan.
_help.code_triggers: Words/regex in the request that hand the task to coder_model. Edit freely; bad regex is ignored.
_help.deep_triggers: Words/regex in the request that ask deep_model for a plan first.
_help.how_it_flows: Everyday model gets every request. code_triggers -> coder_model for the whole task. deep_triggers or a long request -> deep_model plans, then the everyday model (or heavy_model if the plan is long) carries it out. The everyday model can also call the 'escalate' tool itself. Each new request starts back on the everyday model.
_help.question_triggers: A coding request with these words (and none of job_triggers) is a QUESTION: coder_model answers it in words with no tools, so it can't wander off running commands.
_help.job_triggers: Words that make a coding request a JOB on this laptop (run, install, edit a file...): coder_model keeps its tools. These win over question_triggers.
